thread.title: Best Buy Stock Is Slipping After Analyst Predicts Weak Electronics Sales

author: Barron's
title: Best Buy Stock Is Slipping After Analyst Predicts Weak Electronics Sales
text:
Photograph by Jason Connolly/Getty Images Best Buy will report sales below expectations due to headwinds in the consumer electronics market, according to Bank of America Merrill Lynch.
The firm's analyst Curtis Nagle lowered his rating for Best Buy ( BBY ) shares to Underperform from Neutral, citing deteriorating Bank of America's credit-card spending data trends for the retailer's end markets.
"We are downgrading BBY … on a continued deceleration in industry growth trends and continued caution on key product categories such as TVs, Apple products and gaming," he wrote on Monday. "We are turning more negative as we now see a higher possibility that BBY may see an outright comp miss in 4Q and we believe Street 2019/20 EPS ests are too high."
Nagle also lowered the target price on Best Buy stock to $50 from $70. The lowered target price is lower than the current market price of the stock. Best Buy stock was down 4.6% to $52.85 on Monday. The company declined to comment on the report.
https://asset.barrons.com/dj-mg/dice/barrons-staffpicks-2d590600-c862-4394-b9d3-66b48c376d60/inset.json
Bank of America's credit-card spending data revealed consumer spending for consumer electronics and toys fell 6.3% in November versus the 4% gain on average in the previous four quarters.
"While it's possible that Nov. industry trends are a blip and growth inflects in Dec., even if sequential trends hold through 4Q it would imply that BBY would only comp +0.4% in 4Q which would be below consensus," Nagle wrote. "Given that we see risk in key product categories, we believe weak trends are likely to continue."
The analyst noted how televisions accounted for about 25% of the retailer sales and Apple ( AAPL ) products represented about 10% of revenue, according to his estimates. He said both product categories will likely detract from Best Buy's results.
